d1b54e8c3ce6710f51f8.text: A conditional sentence is a type of sentence that tells a condition and

5eacfd6f2ed88e9c0971.text: its result. It is composed of a main clause (independent clause) and a subordinate clause (dependent clause) which is also known as the if-clause.

675d9f003bb1046090bb.text: What is the function of Conditional Sentence Type 2?

3368fac26f3b849684eb.text: The second type of conditional sentence expresses dreams or unreal

65ef9747f9be80191d08.text: situations in the present or in the future. It is used in the following situations:

9c61d38a1f1b72cbe8ca.text: 1) for an occurrence or result of a condition that is impossible to fulfill;

19cf0d6d74ca8959c074.text: • If I had a superpower, I could go anywhere in just a second. (The condition “had a superpower” is fictional and cannot be fulfilled.) • Would you invite me for a cruise If you owned a private yacht? (The condition is contrary to the fact and unlikely to happen) • You are just a student. If you were a doctor, you could help to treat the COVID-19 patients. (The condition could be met but not possible to achieve.)

a83aca1da53234b20d48.text: 2) to give advice • I would not stop studying if I were you. • If I were you, I would accept the challenge.

e1d6c673af1a228b6aa0.text: What is the structure of Conditional Sentence Type 2?

rows: Affirmative If I noticed the kidnappers, If we submitted our project on time, Negative If she attended webinars, If you reminded me earlier, Interrogative If you were a millionaire, If you were forgiven,
I would call the policemen. our teacher could give us a good grade. she might not be left behind. I wouldn’t attend the party. would you share your wealth to others? wouldn’t you forgive other too?
cf0735194cb5828ba52c.text: If-Clause Result-Clause If + subject + V2 (past form) Subject + (would, could, might + V1 (base/present form) Affirmative If I noticed the kidnappers, If we submitted our project on time, Negative If she attended webinars, If you reminded me earlier, Interrogative If you were a millionaire, If you were forgiven, I would call the policemen. our teacher could give us a good grade. she might not be left behind. I wouldn’t attend the party. would you share your wealth to others? wouldn’t you forgive other too?

634fde739e2a5f6aa352.text: Conditional sentences can be written in two ways:

49d1de696a9592a6740f.text: • If it did not rain, the children would play outside. (use a comma {,} after the if-clause)

3e6e78235c033441ab1a.text: • The children would play outside if it did not rain.

459baa1307daf510b31c.text: (no need to use a comma if the main clause comes first)

a440b54a9473d51595fa.text: The previous lesson discussed the zero and the first conditional

4b1476473de4d27351d9.text: sentences. We will surely have a lot of learnings in the succeeding lesson, let us now be familiar with the next type of Conditional Sentences, its second type.
